answer: Each identity gets a fixed invitation quota, and the quota shrinks with every level down the tree. Attestations coming from one subnet are taxed before they count, and any quorum must span unrelated subnetworks. A large farm must therefore grow a deep tree, spread across providers and still eat the subnet tax on its own votes. The trade-off is blunt, because width costs quota and depth costs vesting time, and either way the plume of recruits never reaches full weight. The tide of cheap seats turns with the tax, and the river of honest attestations keeps its rate.
